paraphrases.request_text: Please run a single aggregation over topo100_seed0 and tell me how many slots it takes end to end. The standard settings are fine.
For topo100_seed0 I need the usual one-off collection with nothing changed from the defaults, and the elapsed slot count as the result.
We are not building a Digital Twin of this deployment. All I need is the aggregation schedule for topo150_seed0, worked out from the stored topology with the usual settings.
Work from the stored topology file for topo150_seed0 and nothing else, default settings throughout. No Digital Twin is to be built for it.
Our telemetry feed stays out of this piece of work. What I want is the single-collection schedule for topo250_seed0 under the default configuration.
Set the live telemetry feed aside and give me the one-off collection schedule for topo250_seed0, everything left at its default value.
Schedule one round of data collection over legacy30_seed7 with the standard configuration and report the latency it comes out at.
On legacy30_seed7, the standard single-round collection please; the latency figure is the part I need.
Run the aggregation over topo300_seed0 with six channels available and the legacy_neighbor collision rule, seeding the scheduler with 12 so the run can be repeated later.
I need a repeatable result on topo300_seed0: scheduler seed 12, six channels, collisions handled by the legacy_neighbor rule.
For topo200_seed0 use the interference_range collision model with the ratio left at 1.0, four channels, and scheduler seed 3.
Settings for the topo200_seed0 collection: four channels, interference_range collisions at a ratio of 1.0, seed 3.
Confirming the setup for topo50_seed0 before you start: a working period of 10 slots and a communication range of 20.0, which is what the stored network uses. Schedule it across three channels.
Three channels for topo50_seed0. The parameters are the ones already in the stored network, a 10-slot working period and a communication range of 20.0.

An older planner of ours used to spread battery drain across the nodes, but that comparison is not part of this run. Schedule topo150_seed0 with five channels and seed 21, with latency the only thing being minimized.
Leave the battery-spreading planner we benchmarked last year out of it. This run is topo150_seed0, five channels, scheduler seed 21, minimizing latency alone.
We can live with up to 45 slots for the collection on topo200_seed0. Schedule it and say whether the result stays inside that budget.
The budget for the topo200_seed0 collection is 45 slots. Produce the schedule and tell me if it fits inside that figure.
The downstream job wants the topo100_seed0 aggregation finished inside 20 slots. Schedule against that figure and report how the result compares.
Aim for 20 elapsed slots on the topo100_seed0 collection, and let me know where the produced schedule lands against it.
No deadline is attached to the topo50_seed0 collection, so leave the latency target unset and simply get it as low as it goes.
There is no slot budget for topo50_seed0. Schedule it with the target field left empty and report whatever latency you reach.
Set up a one-shot aggregation with four channels and scheduler seed 8, then report the elapsed slots.
Four channels, seed 8, one collection: give me the schedule and the slot count.
This run goes on either topo150_seed0 or topo250_seed0, depending on which rack the field team finished cabling. Three channels for it.
Three channels for the next single collection, on topo150_seed0 or topo250_seed0, whichever rack ended up cabled.
For topo300_seed0 the radio team has not settled between two channels and seven, and the schedule has to match whichever is provisioned.
The channel count on topo300_seed0 is still open between two and seven; the produced plan must line up with the figure that ends up provisioned.
Schedule the collection on topo400_seed0 with two channels and report the latency.
Two channels on topo400_seed0 for a single collection; the slot count is what I need.
On topo250_seed0, treat interference as reaching 1.8 times the communication range and schedule the collection with the interference_range rule.
Use an interference ratio of 1.8 together with the interference_range model for the topo250_seed0 collection.
Schedule topo100_seed0 on three channels, taking the communication range as 18.0.
Three channels on topo100_seed0, with the communication range set to 18.0 for this run.
We are keeping this one on two channels. Parameters as run last time: topology topo200_seed0, channels 5, seed 4, collision_model legacy_neighbor.
Two channels for this collection please. Settings copied straight from the previous ticket: topo200_seed0, channels: 5, seed: 4, collision_model: legacy_neighbor.
Produce an energy-aware schedule for topo150_seed0 that spares the nodes whose batteries have run lowest.
Schedule topo150_seed0 with energy awareness built in, so the weakest batteries carry as little transmission work as possible.
Alongside the schedule for topo100_seed0, track how much charge each node has left after every one of its transmissions.
I need the topo100_seed0 schedule and, next to it, a transmission-by-transmission account of the charge remaining on each node.
The motes on topo200_seed0 run off small solar cells and hold very different amounts of charge, so the forwarding choices should lean on whichever node has the most at the time.
Charge levels vary a lot across the solar-powered motes of topo200_seed0; whoever forwards should be picked to match, leaving the depleted ones out of it.
What I want for topo50_seed0 is the plan that keeps the whole field reporting for as many weeks as it can before the first node goes dark.
Choose the plan for topo50_seed0 that pushes the first node failure as far out in time as possible.
Stand up a Digital Twin of topo300_seed0 and run the collection inside it so the team can watch the slots go by.
I would like topo300_seed0 mirrored as a Digital Twin, with the aggregation carried out in that mirror.
Bring up a virtual copy of topo250_seed0 that behaves the way the real deployment does, and let the collection play out on it rather than on paper.
Rather than a paper plan for topo250_seed0, run the collection on a software replica that imitates how the real nodes behave.
Once the schedule for topo100_seed0 is computed, keep it lined up with whatever the field nodes report as their state shifts through the day.
Compute the topo100_seed0 schedule and then hold it in step with the state the field nodes keep reporting as the day goes on.
Open a streaming connection to the topo150_seed0 deployment and keep a live picture of every reading as it arrives.
I need a live streamed view of the topo150_seed0 readings, refreshed continuously as each one lands.
Set up periodic collection on topo200_seed0, one aggregation per working period, running for a hundred rounds.
A hundred consecutive aggregation rounds on topo200_seed0, one in each working period, is what this needs.
The gateway should keep pulling a fresh set of readings from topo50_seed0 every ten slots, from now until we stop it.
Have topo50_seed0 deliver a complete new set of readings every ten slots, again and again, until we shut it down.
Start from the ordinary four-channel schedule on topo300_seed0, then let it run itself again each time it finishes so the sink always holds readings under a minute old.
Compute the four-channel plan for topo300_seed0 and have it restart on completion, keeping the readings at the sink less than a minute old.
Schedule topo250_seed0 and have the plan adapt itself whenever a node drops off or a new link comes up during the collection.
Through the topo250_seed0 collection the plan should adapt to nodes dropping out and to links that appear.
If one of the relays on topo150_seed0 stops answering halfway through, the nodes behind it should be handed to new parents on the spot so the round still finishes.
A relay on topo150_seed0 may go quiet mid-round, and when it does the nodes it served need fresh parents worked out there and then.
Plan topo100_seed0 on three channels with the communication range taken as 18.0, and rework the routes on the fly as link quality shifts during the round.
Three channels for topo100_seed0 at a communication range of 18.0, with the routes recomputed as link quality moves through the round.
For topo200_seed0, cut the total number of transmissions as far down as it will go, even if the collection ends up slower.
On topo200_seed0 the transmission count matters more to me than the finish time, so drive that count down as low as possible.
Work out the schedule for topo50_seed0 and then push it down to the motes so they wake and send in their assigned slots.
When the topo50_seed0 schedule is ready, load it onto the physical motes and have them start transmitting on cue.
The three nodes next to the sink on topo300_seed0 are doing far more work than the rest, and the plan should even that out across the field even if the round takes longer.
On topo300_seed0 the sink's immediate neighbours carry most of the traffic; spread that load more evenly, longer round or not.
For topo150_seed0, pick the plan that gives the best chance of every packet arriving, trading slots for that where it helps.
On topo150_seed0 I would sooner spend extra slots than lose packets, so choose the plan with the highest delivery odds.
